lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Body Signals and Fueling My Day
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: asking an adult about a signal

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 4 — body signals, rest, and food variety
objective: Learners practice a three-part script, naming the signal, describing when it started, and stating what is needed, for telling a trusted adult about a body signal, then apply the script to a specific signal from earlier this week that they noticed but did not mention to anyone.
scenario: The learner recalls one specific body signal noticed earlier this week that went unmentioned at the time, and practices saying a three-part script out loud, as if telling a trusted adult about that exact signal right now.

tasks.directions: Think back over the past several days and pick one signal you remember but did not mention out loud at the time.

prompts.text: Name the specific signal you noticed but did not mention, such as hunger, thirst, tiredness, needing a bathroom break, or feeling too hot or cold, and about when it happened.

tasks.directions: Practice saying the three-part script out loud for the signal you named: name the signal, describe when it started, state what you need.

prompts.text: I said the signal's name first, for example, 'I feel thirsty.'
I described when it started, for example, 'since we came inside.'
I stated what I need, for example, 'can I get a drink of water.'
I practiced saying all three parts in order without skipping one.

tasks.directions: Pick a different signal than the one you just practiced.

prompts.text: Write the three-part script for a different signal than the one you practiced, choosing one you have not used yet: hunger, thirst, tiredness, bathroom need, or feeling too hot or cold.

tasks.directions: Think about the three parts of the script you just practiced.

prompts.text: Describe which of the three parts felt hardest, naming the signal, describing when it started, or stating what you need, and explain why.

remediation: If a learner skips straight to a request without naming the signal or when it started, such as saying only 'can I have a snack,' reteach with a fill-in-the-blank sentence frame that forces the three parts to appear in order before the sentence is considered complete.
extension: Have the learner teach the three-part script to someone else by writing out an example conversation that uses all three parts for a brand-new signal.
